### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-print`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/vitest.config.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via printRecordToFile (symbol, a method of class PrintService))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-print/vitest.config.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **4** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `d2071413c8515bc2166bcd38151bb7d44fdb25d5` — the merge of head `4d45f050d3851b9bc3e43494965494db0e3b6db4` into base `bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin d2071413c8515bc2166bcd38151bb7d44fdb25d5 && git checkout d2071413c8515bc2166bcd38151bb7d44fdb25d5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 4d45f050d3851b9bc3e43494965494db0e3b6db4 && git checkout -B drift-repro bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0 && git merge --no-ff 4d45f050d3851b9bc3e43494965494db0e3b6db4

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs bbc7e037f3af837d4d1302177df5f434f2c239c0` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · repo:objectstack#3 · head 4d45f050 · 2026-11-24T00:57Z

L1: ACCEPT
Head-sha: `4d45f050d3851b9bc3e43494965494db0e3b6db4`
Card: #35049 · claim 7101624668 · order: seat route (card option 2: default filename from the ADR-0079 display value, sanitised; explicit `filename` wins; fallback `<page>-<recordId>.pdf`; no spec key).

### Checklist
- **Shape:** `l1-face` CLEAN, 13 items. Draft, base `main`, first line `Fixes #35049`, no closing keyword next to another card. The PR delivers the whole seat route, so `Fixes` is right.
- **Checks at this head:** 55 check-runs. 40 success, 15 skipped (UI, opt-in, queue-only and dogfood-shard jobs, all expected skips), 0 failed, 0 pending. Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check: success. `mergeable_state` clean.
- **Declarations:** `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` in the body and the changeset; they match the claim. My reading agrees. `PrintRecordRequest` keeps its shape: only the TSDoc of `filename` is reworded. No file under `packages/spec/**` is in the diff. The new import (`resolveDisplayField` and `DisplayNameObjectMeta` from `@objectstack/spec/data`) only uses symbols spec already exports through `./data`. None of the four contract faces is touched, so no L2 is owed.
- **Changeset:** `@objectstack/service-print: patch`. That package is published and is the only one whose `src/**` moved. Patch follows `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Scope:** five files sit inside the claim's surface (`service-print/src/**`, the docs page, the changeset). The two declared deviations are the dogfood files `print-service-archive` and `print-service-named-page` and the alias line in `service-print/vitest.config.ts`. I read all three as inside the claim's own "and its tests": they are service-print's own dogfood tests and its test config. The dogfood pins asserted the old default and would have broken in the queue's dogfood shards. The alias is what `check:test-source-alias` requires for the new import. No claim amendment is owed.
- **Premise:** the old line was `req.filename ?? \`${req.page}-${req.recordId}.pdf\``, and `refuseUnlessReadable` read the row as the caller and threw it away. Both confirmed against the base diff.
- **Order's constraints, each met in the diff:**
  - (a) No second read: the row comes from `readAsCaller`, the existing caller-context `findOne`. The unit test pins `findOne` called once, with `context === USER`.
  - (b) Object metadata comes from `engine.registry.getObject`, the same registry the files opt-in reads.
  - (c) There is no `Record #` floor: a blank, missing, non-scalar or sanitised-to-empty value falls back to `<page>-<recordId>.pdf`. Five cases pin this.
  - (d) The name is sanitised and capped at 100 code points, which keeps it inside `sys_attachment.file_name` maxLength 255. The attachment service has no sanitiser to reuse; the body names `attachFileAs`, `buildKey` and `contentDispositionValue`.
  - (e) Collision measured on a real showcase boot: two prints give the same name, two distinct committed `sys_file` rows and two attachments. Nothing is refused or overwritten.
  - (f) An explicit `filename` passes through verbatim (pinned).
- **Display value vs `resolveRecordDisplayName`:** `defaultPrintFilename` reads the same field (`resolveDisplayField`: `nameField` ?? `displayNameField` ?? derived). It drops only the `Record #` floor, as the order asked, and also treats non-scalar values as empty, which is stricter. Field-level security: the row is the read door's answer to the caller, so a hidden column is absent and falls back to the old name; a masked column yields its mask. Neither leaks a value.
- **Docs and changeset, read sentence by sentence:**
  - `content/docs/ui/print-pages.mdx` new paragraph: title field (`nameField` or derived), the four hygiene rules, the 100-character cut, the fallback example `invoice_document-inv_1.pdf`, explicit-wins, two prints and two attachments. Each matches `safeFileBase` / `defaultPrintFilename` and the dogfood case. The code-sample result line `INV-0001.pdf` is consistent.
  - Changeset bullets 1–4 and the "Visible change" line: each matches the code.
  - No other page states the old default. I grepped `content/`, `skills/`, `service-print/README.md` and `packages/spec/src` describes for `<page>-<recordId>` and `_print-` style names; the only remaining hits are the fallback sentences.
- **Tests:** real commands with output. Unit: 131/131 under the verify lock on this head. The ablation went 6 red, and only the display-name cases; fallback and explicit stayed green, so the new tests catch the change. Dogfood: 16/16 on the two touched files with the dogfood closure built. CI Test Core 1–10/10: success on this head. My own local vitest re-run did not start (this container has no built `@objectstack/spec` dist), so I rely on CI and the dev's output. NOT MEASURED locally.
- **Dogfood battery:** not owed (no `!`, no narrowing arm). Dogfood Regression Gate shards run in the queue.

### Findings
Must-fix: none. Should-fix: none.

Nits (no user harm; recorded here, the seat decides whether any gets a card):
- **N1:** `safeFileBase` keeps Unicode format and bidi controls (U+200B–U+200F, U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069). A display name `Invoice<U+202E>exe.pdf` is stored as `Invoice<U+202E>exe.pdf` (the `.pdf` is stripped, then re-added), which displays as `Invoicefdp.exe`. The real extension is always `.pdf`, so this cannot disguise an executable, only make a PDF look odd. Low effect. A one-character-class addition (`\p{Cf}` → removed) would close it.
- **N2:** the trailing-`.pdf` strip runs before the 100-character cut. A value whose cut lands right after an inner `.pdf` (96 chars + `.pdf tail`) yields `….pdf.pdf`. Cosmetic.
- **N3:** Windows device names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1` …) pass through, e.g. `CON.pdf`. Browsers already rename these on save. Cosmetic.

### Landing notes
`Fixes #35049`: merging closes the card. `pm:dispatched` comes off at close-out as usual. `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 36801` at this head: NOT governed, 0 of 7 paths, 206 changed lines (≤ 3000).
